spans.text: Berlin.
As the lock disengages with a "ka-click", the door to the building slowly opens.
Several lights come on within the dark room.
Zzzzt—
The holographic image of a man appears in the doorway.
Good afternoon, Commander.
Good day, Sir.
You seem a little stiff, Commander.
...Well, not every Griffin Commander has the chance to meet you in person.
I've heard my fair share of rumors about you.
Rumors are just that—rumors.
Right now, I am just an old man, performing some insignificant administrative work.
You can think of me as an ordinary senior citizen, Commander. We are much closer than you imagine.
But how could I do that, Sir? After all, you're...
Just call me "Griffin", Commander.
I hope we can be less formal around each other while we're in private.
Um... Alright, Mr...Griffin.
(Chuckles)
While this is a memorable first meeting, I regret that I can only speak to you in this manner.
I hope you are not too offended.
No, of course not.
Thank you for being so understanding, Commander.
I, too, have heard a lot about you.
At first, I thought someone like yourself, who has been on the battlefield many times, would have the indelible scent of bloodthirst and murder about them.
But it seems to me that you are simply a kind and polite young person.
I have not been through a fraction of what you have experienced.
And I do not wish to become like my enemies.
Haha, do pardon the ramblings of an old man.
I am simply delighted to see you.
Kryuger has always had a good eye for talent, and I have always favored useful and capable individuals.
Please excuse this bad habit of mine.
Sir.
Ah yes, please, sit down. No need to be so stiff.
Let us move on to the main subject, Commander.
Of course.
Now then, before we begin...
Commander, I believe you have already encountered this person.
Indeed, I have found Machlian... However, there are many things about her which do not match the data provided.
Before conclusive evidence is available, I would not recommend considering her and the person in the picture to be one and the same.
Griffin smiles.
You ARE a sharp one, Commander. Kryuger's opinion of you was not inflated.
Indeed, the person in the picture is not the Machlian whom you've met.
Rather, she is the Paradeus agent who was planted by Ange's side in Bremen. She stole the name of Morridow and infiltrated our government.
For the sake of convenience, let us continue calling her "Morridow".
So is Machlian Morridow?
Or...are they two identical-looking women?
That is what I hope you will find out.
I have also arranged a consultant for you regarding this problem.
A consultant?
I believe you will be very happy to fight side-by-side with Captain Angelia Tsoi.
Ange? She's in Berlin too?
Perhaps it is time the two of you finally met.
I am sure you have a lot to ask her about Bremen and Morridow.
Alright, I see.
Thank you... Truth to be told, Ange is my most reliable friend.
Indeed, your most reliable friends are often found by your side, Commander.
I hope that after the two of you compare notes, you can become a capable agent for us in Berlin.
You want me to investigate Paradeus' plans for Germany?
You should begin by looking into Machlian. I believe your efforts will be fruitful.
I imagine you have already noticed the anomalies in Bohnsdorf.
...The villagers seemed to be worshipping Machlian in a strange fashion.
Their religious and cult-like behavior certainly matches up with Paradeus' modus operandi.
Their sermons also validated my suspicion... Paradeus' influence is spreading, and I am sure it is already deeply rooted.
Hm, what else have you learned?
Also, there's Machlian... Or should I say Morridow, or whatever her real identity is.
It seems Paradeus values her greatly.
When we were fleeing with her, not only did the villagers come out in force to stop us, Paradeus also dispatched large numbers of troops to cut off our escape.
That was definitely not an act. Their fixation on Machlian is genuine.
Apart from information about Machlian, our previous recon attempts even uncovered the presence of a high-ranking Nyto.
However, she did not engage us directly during the latest confrontation.
Whatever the reason, they were very unwilling to let Machlian fall into our hands.
Fortunately, we chose to infiltrate them and managed to safely extract her by taking advantage of the enemy's slack security measures.
You have done very well, Commander.
Kryuger was right about you. You've served up quite a surprise for your first mission.
Er... Thank you for the praise.
Since Machlian is so important to Paradeus, we can make full use of the importance which they attach to her in order to gain more leads.
I give you full discretion over how to handle this matter, Commander. I can think of nobody else who is as reliable and understands Paradeus as well as you do.
...I understand.
Paradeus' activities are growing more frequent throughout Germany.
The incident in Bremen was only one of many such cases.
Especially now that bloody William has finally managed to extend his claws into Berlin.
What is this William person like?
I came here to look into this very matter.
All we know from his actions is that he is very highly placed. Otherwise there is no way to explain how he can mobilize so many resources.
I still do not know what he is planning, but I am certain that he will stop at no means to disrupt our...endeavors.
He has even orchestrated several terrorist attacks towards that end.
I will spare no effort in my investigation. but if we end up having to face Paradeus head-on like we did before...
I fear our current forces are somewhat insufficient.
I would very much like to personally provide you with support.
However, my current duties will not permit me to do so... Which is why I seek your understanding and forgiveness, Commander.
I will not let the opportunities created by your previous efforts go to waste.
You flatter me.
Still, I will assist you to the best of my ability.
I hope you enjoy the temporary command post I have prepared for you. The facilities here are quite comprehensive and you may make free use of everything here.
In addition...
Perosa, you and Squad Griffin will be under the Commander's authority from now on. I want you to give the Commander your full support in all future operations.
Yes, Sir!
...Thank you for your help. However...
I do not know if I can stop Paradeus' schemes by myself.
Nevertheless, I believe you will try with all your might.
That's the way you've always done it, no?
Do not underestimate yourself, Commander.
The things you have accomplished would be miracles in the eyes of others.
...I understand.
Something still seems to be weighing on your mind.
I might be mistaken, but could it be that I have not yet won your trust?
No...how could that be?
It's just... Perhaps going through so much has left me a little high-strung.
It is good to be suspicious, and I am willing to use my actions to help quell your suspicions.
Kryuger has mentioned your opinions many times before.
Perhaps we might not be completely in alignment, but our ideals are one and the same.
...To be the "shining beacon in a brave new world"?
Everything we do is for the future of ourselves and this world.
Still, I spent a lot of time thinking when I learned that our company had the same motto as the Rossartrist movement.
What did you think about?
I thought about what I ought to be doing.
How I could help our country, our society, and our world free itself from the crappy circumstances we're in.
A revolutionary needs an appropriate philosophy. I believe we will get along very well.
I'm not too sure about that, Mr. Griffin.
Rossartrism paints a beautiful picture of the world.
But can people really unite and understand each other?
...Perhaps I shouldn't keep you in the dark.
Do you want to know how I truly feel about this?
Please, by all means.
My answer is...they cannot.
Men will never be able to stand united or understand each other forever.
What...
That is why this world needs order. It needs rules that will FORCE them to unite, to guide them towards understanding each other.

Those who cause division must be punished. Those who help each other must be rewarded. Only the existence of such behavior-shaping rules will allow mankind to right its wrongs and return the world to its intended order.
Mr. Rossartre was a great pioneer, but he was an idealist.
Idealism cannot help us build an ideal world. We must take responsibility for the consequences of our actions.
We must build a world order that benefits all of humanity, and to that end we will pay any price.
And it will be up to "you" to build and dictate the order of the world?
It is the heart of man that decides the order of the world. We are merely servants of mankind's interests.
...Your answer is a little different from what I expected.
Speaking the truth is the best way of dealing with intelligent people.
If slogans alone could bring about revolutions, then why would we need to speak to each other here?
I have one last question.
Go ahead.
When we reach the end of this road and look back on the things we've sacrificed to get there...
Will justice and decency be among them?
Commander, do you know what fables are?
...Fables?
"The hedgehog, who serves absolute truth, reduces the world to one organizing principle, raises his spines all over, and staunchly resists all other views."
"The cunning and mercurial fox rides the waves of tumultuous times, narrowing his eyes and discerning the discordant voices that can reshape the world."
The hedgehog and the fox... It sounds more like philosophy.
I will not clarify your doubts right now, just as I do not expect you to clarify mind either.
But someday... You will make a choice of your own.
...Perhaps.
In that case, I hope you will bring us good news, Commander.
I have an important meeting that I need to attend, so I will bid you farewell for now.
Yes, Sir.
Griffin executes a gentlemanly bow and switches off the holographic projection.
The Commander's eye falls on the chessboard laid out on the table. What kind of game awaits him this time?
...So Ange is in Berlin too?
Commander, I just received an encrypted message.
Got it.
I take the communicator from her and play back the message.
Hi, Commander. Long time no see.
A familiar face appears on the communicator, though Ange looks a lot more haggard than before.
Still, for some reason, it feels incredibly comforting to see someone I know I can count on.
By the time you see this message, you'll probably have met "that guy".
I'm sure you're bursting with questions—so am I.
So come and meet me, Commander.
I'll be waiting for you at Athena's Owl at 3pm today.
And just to make it clear, I hate people who don't show up on time.
